text_blocks.snippet: Dmitri Mendeleev, a Russian chemist, created the first recognizable periodic table in 1869.

list.snippet: Arranged elements by increasing atomic weight.
Grouped elements with similar chemical and physical properties.
Left empty spaces for elements that had not been discovered yet.
Predicted properties of those missing elements accurately, which proved his theory was correct.
Julius Lothar Meyer: A German chemist who published a similar table independently around the same time in 1864 and 1868, but did not predict new elements.
John Newlands: An English chemist who arranged elements by atomic weight and noted repeating patterns.
Henry Moseley: Later rearranged the modern table by atomic number instead of atomic weight in 1913.
